ORIGINAL ISSUE: selection-list-service: S7 authorization was never implemented — 38 acceptance tests are correctly red
## Summary

The `Selection list service (integration/acceptance)` suite went from **134 failing / 6 passing** to **38 failing / 102 passing** in #1180. The remaining 38 are **not** a CI defect. They are the independent acceptance suite correctly reporting service behaviour that was never built.

All numbers below are **measured**, by running the CI job's exact sequence (`dist/db/migrate.js` → `dist/index.js` with `NODE_ENV=test FLAGS_FORCE_ON=fuzefront.selection-lists.service` → `tests/selection-list-service npm test`) against a real PostgreSQL. They are not inferred from a log.

## The headline: authorization is a stub

`grep -rn "TODO(S7)" services/selection-list-service/src/routes/` returns **12 markers**:

| File | Markers |
|---|---|
| `src/routes/lists.ts` | 7 (including the file-level `// TODO(S7): add permit.check() before each mutating operation.`) |
| `src/routes/items.ts` | 7 |
| `src/routes/quota.ts` | 2 |

Only `src/routes/access.ts` actually calls `requireAuthzCheck`. Every other route performs **no authorization check at all** — it authenticates the caller and then serves the request.

Second, related gap: **`grantListOwner()` in `src/middleware/authz.ts:244` has no call site anywhere in `src/`.**

```
$ grep -rn "grantListOwner" services/selection-list-service/src/
src/middleware/authz.ts:35://     consulted for authorization. It is updated by grantListOwner() and
src/middleware/authz.ts:45://     `grantListOwner()` and `src/routes/access.ts`'s PUT/DELETE handlers.
src/middleware/authz.ts:223:// grantListOwner — grant list-owner via the Security API + upsert mirror row
src/middleware/authz.ts:244:export async function grantListOwner(
```

Three references, all of them comments or the definition itself. So creating a list never makes the creator its owner and never writes the `selection_list_access` mirror row.

## Measured breakdown of the 38

### A. No authorization on the routes — 25 tests

`security/authz.test.ts` walks the full role matrix. Every "cannot → 403" case receives **201/200** instead, because no route consults an authorization decision.

```
● list-viewer role › cannot: add_value → 403
    Expected: 403
    Received: 201
```

Affected: `list-viewer` (7), `list-contributor` (5), `list-translator` (6), `list-editor` (3), `list-owner` (1), plus:

- `id is not a capability › a user with no grant on a list gets 404 (not 403) when reading it` — got **200**. A list is currently readable by any authenticated member of the org. This is the one with a security consequence rather than only a missing-feature consequence.
- `GET .../access — authorization › a list-editor cannot read the access grants (requires manage_access)` — got **200**.

### B. The creator is never granted list-owner — 5 tests

Direct consequence of the unwired `grantListOwner()`:

- `grants list-owner to the creator automatically` — grant undefined
- `GET .../access — pagination › returns the pagination envelope with items + page` — `page.items.length` is **0**, expected ≥ 1
- `Last-owner protection › demoting the only list-owner ... 409` — got **200** (there is no owner row to be the last one)
- `Last-owner protection › revoking the only list-owner ... 409` — got **200**
- `PUT .../access/{userId} › grant returns the correct AccessGrant shape` — `grant.list_id` is `undefined`

The last-owner guard is currently **vacuous**: `countActiveOwners()` reads a mirror that nothing populates, so it always returns 0 and the 409 never fires.

### C. Quota ceilings are not enforced — 3 tests

The CI job sets `TEST_QUOTA_ORG_LISTS=3` / `TEST_QUOTA_LIST_ITEMS=5`; **nothing in `src/` reads either name** (`grep -rn "TEST_QUOTA" src/` is empty). The ceiling stays at whatever `quota.service.ts` defaults to, so:

- `org_lists quota enforcement › ... → 403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — got **201**
- `list_items quota enforcement › ... → 403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — got **201**
- `Concurrent quota enforcement (advisory lock) › parallel creates at the ceiling` — 8 of 8 succeeded against a ceiling of 5

Note this means **the advisory-lock concurrency guard is currently unexercised** — the test cannot reach the ceiling it is meant to race at.

### D. Route-behaviour gaps — 5 tests

| Test | Expected | Got | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/selection-lists — status filter › status=all returns both` | 200 | 400 `status must be one of: active, archived` | `src/routes/lists.ts:211` omits `all`; check which the spec intends |
| `locale validation › unsupported locale value returns 400 (not a silent fallback)` | 400 | **200** | silently falls back instead of rejecting |
| `PATCH .../items/{itemId} › can update label without touching code` | 200 | **500 "An unexpected error occurred."** | a real unhandled error, worth reproducing first |
| `DELETE .../items/{itemId} — archive vs purge › cannot purge a list that still has non-archived items — 409` | 409 | **204** | purge succeeds where the spec says conflict |
| `PUT .../access/{userId} — org membership › granting access to a user outside the org returns 400` | 400 | **200** | cross-org grant accepted |

## Also worth deciding

The job carries `continue-on-error: true`, so none of this blocks master. Once A–D are closed, that line should come off and the job should become a required context — otherwise the suite goes on reporting into a room that tolerates it.

## What was already fixed (not part of this issue)

In #1180, for the record so nobody re-diagnoses it:

- The release flag defaults OFF with Unleash as its only source of truth, so every route answered `404 Service not enabled.` in CI. Fixed with the repo's existing `FLAGS_FORCE_ON` hatch, hard-gated to non-production.
- `src/db/knexfile.ts` had no `test` environment, so `NODE_ENV=test` resolved to `undefined` and the service could not connect.
- **`src/middleware/auth.ts` read `userId`/`orgId` only** — neither the name its own `openapi.yaml` `bearerAuth` publishes (`organization_id`, `sub`) nor a shape any real emitter produces with both. 93 of the 134 failures were this one claim-name mismatch.
- Three acceptance assertions read `^sl_`/`^sli_` where `openapi.yaml` pins `^front_sl_`/`^front_sli_`.
